name: Lumen & Lathe — Spire Tasting Laboratory
creator: Chef Emiliano Achebe-Sørensen
description: Occupying the 91st floor of the Cassian Tower in the Spire's commercial district, Lumen & Lathe is a 14-seat tasting laboratory where Chef Emiliano Achebe-Sørensen presents a single annually revised 22-course menu exploring what he calls 'the archaeology of appetite' — each dish reconstructed from pre-Synthesis culinary records, then deliberately destabilized through geneware-grown ingredient substitution. A reservation requires a Φ2,200 deposit and a six-month waitlist; the menu itself costs Φ4,800 per person excluding the neural-enhanced flavor pairing service (an additional Φ900), which uses BCI micro-stimulation to heighten specific taste receptors during each course. The restaurant operates at a deliberate loss as a prestige project for its Spire patron, Haruki Ferreira-Vance, who uses it as a client entertainment venue.
cultural_impact: Lumen & Lathe's annual menu releases are treated as cultural events by the Spire class, and Achebe-Sørensen's published menus circulate widely in pirated neural-feed form among food enthusiasts in lower tiers who can experience the documentation but never the food itself. The restaurant inadvertently became a symbol of the Synthesis Gap — the distance between those who eat for pleasure and those who eat for survival.
controversy: In 2214, the 'Dust Course' — a recreation of pre-Collapse wheat bread using geneware grain analogs — was condemned by Shelf food activists as obscene given active grain scarcity in Tier 1-2 zones. Achebe-Sørensen's public response was widely considered inadequate.
story_hooks: A Shelf food journalist receives an anonymous reservation to Lumen & Lathe with a note reading 'eat everything, remember everything' — someone wants a witness inside who won't stay quiet.

One of Achebe-Sørensen's geneware ingredient suppliers has been quietly replaced by a corponation subsidiary, and a sous chef suspects at least two courses now contain compounds not listed on the menu.
The annual menu for 2226 is rumored to include a course made from an ingredient that cannot legally be served in Meridian 88, and the reservation list includes three corporate attorneys.
